summary.name: TernaryCode
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native terminal workspace that shows all your projects and the coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) running in them, and flags which agent is waiting for you.
use_cases: Monitor several coding agents across many projects at once
Know which AI agent is waiting for permission or an answer
Review and merge changes made by an agent
Run agents in separate git worktrees so they don't overwrite each other
Commit, push and open a pull request from reviewed diffs
Let an agent drive a local dev server in a built-in browser panel
summary.what_it_does: TernaryCode is a native app (not Electron) that hosts a grid of real terminals, one per project, and tracks the status of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode agents through their hooks. Agents waiting for input are listed at the top of the sidebar, navigable with a keyboard shortcut. A Code drawer shows files an agent changed with line markers and language server support, and a Review view shows diffs with options to commit, push and open pull requests. It also includes a browser panel agents can drive, and viewers for PDF, Office files, CSV and images.
notable: Status from agent hooks shows which agent needs permission, is working, or has finished
Native app with no Electron or web wrapper, using egui and alacritty_terminal
Agents can be started in their own git worktree and reviewed or merged from the app
No account, no telemetry; only checks GitHub for updates
caveats: Builds are not yet notarized or code-signed, so macOS and Windows show security warnings on install
Browser panel on Linux requires WebKitGTK 4.1; without it pages open in the default browser
Agent status for Antigravity CLI is only 'Active' because it has no hooks yet
